ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The resultant Ampere force on the entire wire frame is zero

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a right-triangular closed conducting wire frame labeled a, b, c; the left side is the vertical side ab, the lower side is the horizontal side bc, and the hypotenuse is ac; the region where the triangle is located is filled with “×” symbols, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward, and B is also marked in the figure. The angle at c is marked as 30°. The question stem states that the direction of the current in the wire frame is clockwise. Then reason: For the entire closed wire frame in a uniform magnetic field, the resultant Ampere force can be written as F合 = I∮dℓ × B. Since the magnetic field B is the same everywhere, it can be taken outside the integral sign, giving F合 = I(∮dℓ) × B. The vector displacement sum around the closed circuit ∮dℓ = 0, so F合 = 0. The 30° angle and the clockwise current direction will only affect the specific direction of the force on each side, and do not change the conclusion that the resultant Ampere force on the entire closed wire frame in a uniform magnetic field is zero.
